images.title: One third, two sixths
images.purpose: Show that each third of a strip splits into 2 sixths, so 1/3 and 2/6 of the same strip end at the same fold.
images.composition: Two paper strips of the same length, one above the other with a wide gap, and one bracket under the lower strip.
images.exact_structure: Upper strip: cut into 3 equal parts, the left 1 part filled teal #0072B2. Lower strip: exactly the same length, left edges lined up, cut into 6 equal parts, the left 2 parts filled amber #E69F00. The fold at the end of the teal part lines up exactly with the fold at the end of the second amber part. One reddish purple #CC79A7 curly bracket under the 2 amber parts. Exactly 2 strips, 3 thirds, 6 sixths, 1 bracket.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
strips of different lengths, or the teal part and the two amber parts ending at different places
images.takeaway: Each third is 2 sixths, so 1/3 and 2/6 are the same length.
images.description: Two equal strips, one in 3 equal parts with 1 shaded teal, one in 6 equal parts with 2 shaded amber; the shaded parts end at the same fold, and 1/3 = 2/6 is written below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the teal third and then at the two amber sixths under it, and say they end at the same fold.

image_decisions.why: Seeing a third split into two sixths on equal strips is a picture idea; one image carries it.
